clue.text: No I dressing room at the old Royal Court?

definitions.text: No I dressing room at the old Royal Court?

parts.words: No I dressing room at the old Royal Court?
parts.note: the dressing room kept for the leading performer, the number one, could be called the star's room; the same two words name a notorious Tudor and Stuart court

explanation.surface: A theatre's number-one dressing room at the historic Royal Court Theatre in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'I' is the newspaper's Roman numeral one. 'Royal Court' looks like the London theatre, but it means a court of the monarch: the Star Chamber sat at Westminster until 1641.
explanation.definitionFit: The Star Chamber was an English court of law under the Tudor and Stuart monarchs, notorious for arbitrary judgments.

clue.text: Be inclined to nurse

definitions.meaning: to have a tendency or leaning towards something
to look after someone who is ill

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers having a leaning (tend to agree) and caring for a patient (tend the wounded).

clue.text: Dismissed after one run? What a beating!

indicators.note: after says the word for dismissed follows the letter for the run

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run
a batsman who is dismissed is out

explanation.surface: A cricketer out after scoring just one run: a thrashing indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a batsman out for one is apt: a rout is a crushing defeat, which 'What a beating!' exclaims.
explanation.definitionFit: A rout is an overwhelming defeat, a thorough thrashing.

clue.text: Double-edged weapon consort presented to Henry

indicators.note: presented to puts the consort's name after the letter for Henry, as something handed over to him

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort

explanation.surface: A royal consort hands a two-edged weapon to King Henry.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a king, but it is the physics unit, abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberd (here in its older spelling) is a pole weapon with an axe blade and spike, cutting on more than one edge.

clue.text: Pet poem of Kipling in medium frequency

indicators.note: in says the poem's title sits inside the frequency abbreviation

parts.note: MF is the radio abbreviation for medium frequency
If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem

explanation.surface: A favourite Kipling poem broadcast on medium wave radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a favourite, an adjective for the poem, but it is the noun meaning a sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is a fit of sulking or peevishness, as is a miff.

clue.text: See missile that goes into orbit

definitions.meaning: to look at closely, to stare at
the orbit is the eye socket, and the ball sitting in it is the organ of sight

explanation.definitionFit: To eyeball is to look hard at something, and the eyeball is the globe lodged in the bony orbit of the skull.

clue.text: Taxes paid late

parts.note: late here means dead: these taxes fall due on the estate of someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone settling their tax bill after the deadline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' suggests overdue payment; it means deceased, as in 'the late Mr Smith'.
explanation.definitionFit: Death duties were British taxes levied on a deceased person's estate, the forerunner of inheritance tax.

clue.text: Final entrance ofstage-player in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its appearance altered, so the letters of the player are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor in costume making a last entrance onto the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs 'of' and 'stage-player' together; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The pearly gates are the gates of heaven, traditionally the last way in at the end of life.

clue.text: Fellow taking summer abroad, for the carnival

parts.note: été is the French word for summer, a foreign word

explanation.surface: A man spending the summer overseas to enjoy the carnival.
explanation.definitionFit: A fête is a festive outdoor celebration or gala, like a carnival.

clue.text: Downright incompetent?

definitions.meaning: lacking the qualifications or skill for a job

explanation.definitionFit: An unqualified success is an absolute one, and someone unqualified lacks the credentials for the work.

clue.text: Commotion makes one run on street

indicators.note: in an across answer on puts the letters for one and run after the street abbreviation

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when someone goes jogging down the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a disturbance or fuss, a commotion.

clue.text: So mean, near being punched?

parts.note: close means near
fisted suggests struck with a fist

explanation.surface: Someone so stingy they nearly get hit for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' is a link word. 'Near' also means stingy in British slang, which adds to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fisted person is stingy, unwilling to part with money, as a mean person is.

clue.text: Dark ale for hotel-worker working late?

parts.note: night is the dark part of the day
porter is a dark ale

explanation.surface: A dark beer ordered for the hotel staff member on the late shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark ale' reads as one item, porter, but 'Dark' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A night porter staffs a hotel's front desk through the night.

clue.text: Lie about, guaranteed some rest

indicators.note: about means the letters of the word lie are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain, guaranteed

explanation.surface: Lying around is a sure way to get some rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LIE into LEI.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time, a spell of relaxation away from work.

clue.text: Some inherit house, here by the Thames

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone inheriting a riverside house by the Thames.
explanation.walkthrough: ERITH is a town in south-east London on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Erith lies on the south bank of the Thames in the London Borough of Bexley.

clue.text: Standard time for a charity collection?

parts.note: a standard is a flag or banner
a day is a period of time

explanation.surface: The usual time set aside for a charity fundraising drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like 'usual'; it is a banner. A British flag day is when collectors give donors small paper flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A flag day is a day of street fundraising for a charity, with donors given a token flag or sticker.

clue.text: Girl strangely naif about love

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the letter for love
strangely says the letters of naif are rearranged into an odd order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl who is oddly innocent where love is concerned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns NAIF into FINA, and 'about' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiona is a girl's name of Scottish origin.

clue.text: Track of territory's first corncrake

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word territory

parts.note: the corncrake is a bird of the rail family

explanation.surface: Following the trail of the first corncrake in a bird's territory.
explanation.walkthrough: Corncrake is a specific example of a rail, a family of marsh birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A trail is a path or the track left by something moving.

clue.text: Hunting cry heard in night-club district

definitions.meaning: a shout huntsmen give when a hare is sighted
a London area known for its bars, clubs and theatres

explanation.walkthrough: 'heard in' is a link: the old hunting cry is said to have given the district its name. SOHO is in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: So-ho was a cry of hare coursing, and Soho is the London entertainment quarter thought to be named after it.

clue.text: Classicwalkoftailless ermine

indicators.note: tailless means the last letter of the word for an ermine is cut off

parts.note: the ermine is a stoat in its white winter coat

explanation.surface: A classical colonnade walked by a stoat with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The page runs the words together. 'Classic' points to ancient Greece, where a stoa was a covered walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a roofed colonnade in ancient Greek architecture where people strolled and talked.

clue.text: Compensate for when mouse ran down

definitions.meaning: to make amends for a wrong
in the nursery rhyme Hickory Dickory Dock, the clock struck one and the mouse ran down

explanation.walkthrough: Hickory Dickory Dock is an English nursery rhyme: 'The clock struck one, the mouse ran down'.
explanation.definitionFit: To atone is to make amends, and in the rhyme the mouse ran down at one o'clock.

clue.text: Longing endlessly for an analgesic

indicators.note: endlessly says the final letter of the word for longing is dropped

parts.note: aspiring means longing or hoping for something

explanation.surface: Someone longing endlessly for a painkiller.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirin is a common painkilling drug, acetylsalicylic acid.

clue.text: Attractive fellow leaves a print

indicators.note: leaves means the letter for fellow departs from the word for attractive

parts.note: fetching means attractive

explanation.surface: A handsome man walks out, leaving behind a print.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' looks like a noun or a verb meaning departs with a print left; it removes F.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from a metal plate whose design has been bitten in with acid.

clue.text: Dandified Pop, perhaps, caught in angle

indicators.note: caught in says the rearranged letters are held inside the word for angle

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of pop could be in some other order

explanation.surface: A vain, dressy father photographed from a flattering angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns POP into OPP, which goes inside FISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Foppish describes someone overly concerned with fine clothes, like a dandy.

clue.text: Adapted the tale of the competitor?

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: A rewritten story about a sporting contestant.
explanation.definitionFit: An athlete is a sports contestant, someone who competes in events.

clue.text: Active agent embracing redhead

indicators.note: embracing says the word for agent wraps around the letter

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
the head of the word red is R

explanation.surface: A lively secret agent hugging a red-haired companion.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means nimble and energetic, especially of an older person.

clue.text: Start to plunder old Chester

indicators.note: Start to means only the opening part of the word for plunder is kept

parts.note: to devastate is to lay waste or ravage

explanation.surface: Beginning to loot the ancient city of Chester.
explanation.walkthrough: DEVA was the Roman fort at Chester, a city in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Deva was the Roman name for the legionary fortress that became the city of Chester.

clue.text: Hilary, for example, in Outer Mongolia

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone named Hilary visiting Outer Mongolia, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Hilary looks like a person; it is the spring term at Oxford and of the English law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary is the name of the academic and legal session beginning in January in England.

clue.text: Look at small tin

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Examining a little tin can.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan is to examine or look over something.

clue.text: Excellence shown in front of the cardinal?

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before or in front of
a cardinal is addressed as His Eminence

explanation.surface: Superior quality displayed before a senior churchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pre-eminence is the quality of surpassing all others, superiority.

clue.text: Peaceful flat

explanation.definitionFit: An even temper is calm, and an even surface is level.

clue.text: Big picture shows general breaking down before men on square

indicators.note: breaking down says the letters of general fall apart and reform

parts.note: a T-square is a drawing tool, so square gives T

explanation.surface: A large photo of a general collapsing in front of soldiers on the parade square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking down' turns GENERAL into ENLARGE; MEN and T follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: An enlargement is a photograph printed larger than the original.
